messages:
Ava (support): heads up — acme reported a big latency spike and data-residency alarm. They say Console shows region=eu-west-1 but our traces show serving_region=us-central1. Customer worried about cross-border data and incorrect billing (they were charged EU rates). Correlation id: abc123. Example request attached.

Mike (support-lead): ok—thanks. do we have the raw request/response headers and the API key id? Could be a capacity fallback, or an API-key-scoped region mismatch.

Tara (eng-sre): paste the curl + headers. check for any region override headers (eg. X-Redwood-Preferred-Region / X-Forwarded-Host) and the x-request-id so I can pull the trace. Also include the account id.

Ava (support): here's what customer sent (sanitized):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-🟢" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Preferred-Region: eu-west-1" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4-like","input":"hello"}'
```

Response headers (from their capture):
```
x-request-id: abc123
x-served-region: us-central1
x-consumed-gpu: a100
content-type: application/json
```

Console (customer account page) shows: region label: eu-west-1 (preferred)
Billing invoice shows EU tier pricing.

Ben (eng-runtime): fyi we rolled a small routing policy tweak yesterday to improve burst capacity: it allows cross-pop fallbacks from eu-west to us-central if eu capacity < 20% and latency targets can still be met. BUT there is an unrelated bug where the Console region badge is derived from account.preferred_region metadata rather than actual serving_region in request telemetry. So console can show EU while traffic served elsewhere.

Tara (eng-sre): that matches. @Ben can you check whether the fallback rule is matching this API key/account? also need to verify header propagation for billing pipeline — if billing uses console label, charges could be wrong.

Ava (support): customer trace link: https://traces.internal.redwood/trace/abc123 (internal). They flagged it urgent due to compliance.

Ben (eng-runtime): grabbing trace... quick notes: trace shows route decision: eu-west-1 -> fallback us-central1 due to low available slots at 2024-05-10T14:23:10Z. Serving host: gpu-45.us-central1. Also I see API key meta: preferred_region=eu-west-1, region_lock=false. That explains console label vs actual serving.

Mike (support-lead): action items: 1) SRE: confirm if routing fallback settings are correct / unintended; 2) Runtime: consider changing billing enrichment to use x-served-region header rather than console label; 3) Support: inform customer and open a billing reconciliation. tag finance.

deploy-bot: [deploy-notice] deploy/2026-03-10 routing-tuning (commit: abcdef123) — changed fallback threshold for eu-west.

Tara (eng-sre): repro steps I'm running (please run in your env):
```
# simulate API call with preferred-region header
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-test-xyz" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Preferred-Region: eu-west-1" \
  -H "Host: api.redwood.ai" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4-like","input":"ping"}'
```
Check response headers for `x-served-region` and compare to console/account.preferred_region.

Ben (eng-runtime): additional check — see if the API key has any delegated region override in the key metadata (region_lock vs routing_priority). If region_lock is false we allow fallback. I will patch console to display both preferred_region and last_served_region in the UI and fix the label logic. ETA ~3h for UI patch. Will also add an enrichment step to billing consumer to prefer x-served-region.

Ava (support): repro run (my laptop): I ran Tara's curl with a test key linked to the account. Output: `x-served-region: us-central1`, console still shows eu-west-1. trace id for repro: repro-1718054500. Customer notified that we have a root cause and next steps.

Mike (support-lead): escalating to infra + billing now. opening internal ticket: SUP-5482 with priority P1, assigning @Ben and @Tara. CC finance@redwood.com and legal@redwood.com for residency questions. Customer SLA: promise update in 4 hours.

Ben (eng-runtime): rolling a hotfix for the console label and billing enrichment. I'll add a migration to re-tag past invoice events where served-region != account-region. Tentative ETA 3h for patch, 24h for backfill.

Tara (eng-sre): I'll run synthetic tests across POPs and create an alert when (served_region != account.preferred_region) for >1% of requests per hour. Also validating fallback thresholds — might tighten them for eu-west to reduce cross-border fallbacks.

Ava (support): customer updated: they want confirmation of whether any EU PII left region. we asked infra for a list of request ids served from us-central for that account during the window. will share once we have it. thanks all :pray:

Mike (support-lead): nice work team. keep this thread updated with ticket numbers and any customer-facing wording.

Ben (eng-runtime): note to self: follow-up - add `x-served-region` header to long-term logs and billing events, and add a data-residency flag to invoices when served_region != preferred_region.

Ava (support): closing loop for now — customer told we'll follow up with exact list + billing reconciliation within 4 hours. I'll post the ticket id and customer-facing note when available.
